about: P3.4C-3 run_transition contract corpus. ONE observable behaviour for the real custodian (custodian self-test-run-corpus) and the simulated custodian (test/custodian-run.contract.test.ts). Each scenario runs on a fresh store; unless the scenario says grant:false (or a number of loops) the repository has an 8-loop operator grant. Steps: t (run_transition: run, kind, fields), mint (consume_loop for the run, no implicit open), bind (loop_transition bind with the run's bind nonce, session s-1, process $claude), loop (another loop_transition at the loop's current epoch and revision), replay (re-send an earlier step's exact request, by its requestId), list (list_user_records with every section; data is {protected, loop, run, ...}; summary is computed from run.record), amend (record a protected amendment with disclosure digest `disclosure`; capture.amendment names its record id), decide (prepare a decision at the log's current revision with covered_items `covered` and decided_against `decidedAgainst`; capture.intent names it), commit (commit a captured intent), dropRun (a storage rollback removes the run record), grant (the operator grants `loops` more loops). Fields: an object with $template is that corpus template overlaid (shallowly) with the object's other keys, resolved recursively; the value $omit removes a key. Placeholders: $hex:<c> (64 times the hex digit c), $op:<name> (an operation id captured with capture.op), $amendment:<name>, $nonce, $claude. Processes (OS facts, independent of every field): the originating Claude process ($claude); the engine (the writer of what it sends) and its pipe helper (the connected client) inside its tree; client: outsider = a process outside that tree, ended = $claude has exited, reused = $claude's pid names a later process; writer: other = another process inside the tree (a shell); writerState: gone = the engine process is no longer running, unreadable = the process table cannot be read. caller: operator = the operator surface. expect: ok, code (when ok is false), data (partial match: objects recursively, anything else exactly), present (keys of the result), absent (strings that must not appear in the result), recordKeys (the exact key set of a list step's run.record), recordHas (keys run.record must have), summary (a list step's run.record as: status, runRevision, evidenceEpoch, operations [kind:status], writerAlive [the verdicts the record carries], reviews {id: round:accepted|round:not:reasons+joined|round:running}, items {id: status@revision}, effects {id: [assessment=effect]}, links {id: by=supersededBy;sup=a,b;re=c}, incidents [kind:source], executions [id:status], responses [id:item], replies [id:item]; null when there is no record). P3.4C-4 (version 2): unless the scenario says config:false, the repository also holds the corpus's protected configuration (config.payload, with the Codex installation the runner writes as config.pe describes, a self-test confirmation config.selftest and an acceptance config.acceptance); each runner first checks that the custodian computed config.digests, config.captureRulesDigest and config.codexSha256 exactly (the digest parity oracle). Steps: config (action set | revoke | reconfirm: a prepare at the record's current revision, then commit; set takes the corpus payload with `payload`'s top-level keys replacing its own, a check {"$from": <name>} copying the corpus definition, and `codex` none | variant:<n> replacing the installation), revokeGlobal (kind isolation_acceptance | selftest_confirmation: revoke the scenario's record), recover (the custodian's recovery after a new boot: U1–U5 with U4b). Placeholders: $def:<check> (config.digests), $captureRules, $codexSha, $acceptance (the scenario's acceptance id). A list step also returns the config section; summary.basis maps each review to usable or its basisReason. P3.4C-5 Increment 2 (version 3): a protected review's op_begin RESERVES (template reviewBegin: the source the engine selected its evidence for, selectionSourceId; the target; the offered discussion and amendments; no capture fields and no prompt digest — such claims are ignored) and the custodian captures the review itself: the operation is measuring until a capture step commits it. Unless the scenario says config:false, the corpus also approves a synthetic engine runtime, and the custodian's capture runs only when a step asks. Steps: capture (the reserved operation `of`, captured with the corpus's synthetic capture — a manifest listing context/README.md, that file and a record — of sourceId (default: the reservation's selectionSourceId), stable (default true), or fail: timeout | helper | runtime | cancelled | frame_outside_manifest | frame_hash | withheld; data is the commit's result: operationStatus captured | deduplicated | error | cancelled | interrupted, reason, deduplicatedOf, round), tamper (change a published file of the captured operation `of`, as a bypass would), restart (the custodian restarts in the same boot: the start reconciliation of N5-18). The finish of a captured review names promptDigest and presented (template presented).

config.pe: a 512-byte PE image: zeros, 'MZ' at 0, 0x80 at 0x3C, 'PE' at 0x80, 0x64 0x86 (machine x64) at 0x84

scenarios.name: open: registration needs a grant with a loop left, is idempotent on its declaration, and a terminal run is never re-opened
consume_loop needs the run open; a loop transition ends the loop when its run record is terminal or missing
op_begin and respond are accepted only from the bound session's process tree (D7: correlation, not authentication)
a checks operation: planned checks only, one writer, the execution budgets
a review: the custodian derives acceptance, deduplicates within the evidence epoch, and only an accepted review changes the items
the item table (§4.5): the custodian computes every assessment's effect and the resulting status; a contradicting payload changes nothing
respond: claims against the custodian's item revisions; replies and responses are bound to what the custodian holds
a review presents only amendments the custodian holds, with their disclosure digest (C2 case d)
recover: only once the custodian's process table shows the operation's writer gone; reduce-only

incidents.detail: a check's process tree may survive

scenarios.name: end: terminal and irreversible, from either surface; the run's loop ends with it
budgets: the run's declared budgets under the custodian's hard caps
validation: allowlisted fields, closed enums and strict types; no field conveys authority
error codes are structural: an id or check name that spells a code never selects that code
decision freshness on a protected run (§3.4(2)): the custodian checks the covered items at prepare and their revisions at commit
listing: the run section with its own revision, the custodian's protected answer, and the two projections
P3.4C-4 configuration: a protected run needs the repository's record in force (CONFIG_NOT_HELD, nothing registered); the record's changes are the operator's
P3.4C-4 checks (M3): every planned check that runs names its approved definition; an execution carries the planned one and is recorded under the operation's pin
P3.4C-4 reviews (M4, M11 c): the isolation basis, capture rules and Codex image a review claims must be the held ones; a basis lost during the review is not accepted
P3.4C-4 lifecycle (M11 d/e, M7): after acceptance a revoked, changed or lapsed basis makes a review's basis unusable; recovery after a new boot lapses every record until the operator re-confirms

P3.4C-5 reservation and capture (§3.1, §2.4): the custodian measures the review; identities, deduplication, refused measurements, export integrity, cancellation and the same-boot restart (N5-2, N5-3, N5-16, N5-18)
P3.4C-5 reservation shape: the P3.4C-3 capture shape is gone, the target is validated, the offered bindings are cross-checked; promptDigest and presented belong to a captured review finish

P3.4C-5 Increment 3 check measurement (§4): the custodian measures a checks operation's start and each execution's end itself; claimed identities are ignored; a pending measurement holds the operation
P3.4C-5 Increment 3 measurement recovery: an execution whose end was never measured is recorded unmeasured on recover and on a custodian restart (N5-18); it never counts as fresh
P3.4C-5 Increment 3 protected derivation (§5): over the custodian's own records and measurements; a spend names a fresh implementer-step derivation whose work facts moved (N5-1, N5-14, N5-17)

P3.4C-5 Increment 4 export retention (§3.2, F-2-2): a live run keeps its latest two published exports; failed and deduplicated captures leave nothing; an ended run retires its exports; abandoned staging and orphans are swept; the age bound retires the rest

Phase 4 Increment 2 delegated fix (§3.2, §3.4; N4-4): op_begin binds the boundary, the custodian's baseline capture and an operator-confirmed FIX self-test (never S1); the custodian validates the submitted content itself, rejects every violation, and holds valid content under the digest it computes

Phase 4 Increment 2 delegated fix (N4-5, §3.2 retention): maxFixes refuses a further delegation (none declared: none); a changed baseline export is never vouched for; a fix's writer recovers it; a pending proposal keeps its baseline export until it expires
Phase 4 Increment 2 (TD review): the basis a fix was begun under is re-checked at its finish; delegated-fix paths are ASCII (one case-folding rule); proposal content no run references is swept

Phase 4 Increment 3: the custodian renders the proposal; the owner's confirmation is bound to that rendering and single use; the application consumes it only against an unchanged baseline (FIX_STALE), returns the confirmed content (never kept in the log) and records the custodian's post-apply measurement; the rendering escapes terminal controls

scenarios.name: Phase 4 Increment 3: a rejection closes the proposal; a confirmation expires; an interrupted application is never applied, blocks every other application until reconciled (APPLY_IN_PROGRESS) and is reconciled restore/leave; a changed baseline refuses the commit (CONFIRMATION_CONTENT_MISMATCH); an ended run retires its proposals

outcome.detail: a preimage mismatch at use; nothing was written

scenarios.name: Step 7.1 list_fix_proposals and the guided decision: custodian-held facts per fix (pending, waiting, expired, ineligible), the path from the configuration history resolved to the run's identity; a complete selection prepares only the proposal and rendering reviewed (SELECTION_STALE otherwise, also for another repository's path or identity); one or two expected values, or a value of the wrong type, is MALFORMED_REQUEST; two decisions on one proposal: the first commit wins

Step 7.1 a moved repository and a reused path: the listing offers a fix only at a path that resolves to the run's identity now (unavailable otherwise, with the last recorded path); a selection prepared at a reused path, or at the moved path with the rendering reviewed at the old one, is SELECTION_STALE; listing at the new path makes it selectable again

Step 7.1 legacy records: a run with no configuration pinned at its open, and a repository whose configuration was revoked, are listed from the configuration history (the record on disk is not changed); the existing decision without expected values works as before

has: It authorizes no commit, push, merge, tag or release.

scenarios.name: Step 7.1 the listing bound: at most 50 entries, pending first and the soonest to expire first; exactly 50 is complete; beyond 50 the cut is reported (total, truncated, and the pending fixes it left out, omittedPending), never silent; deciding a listed fix brings the omitted one in; a fix that expires before the listing is no longer pending and does not displace a pending one; a listed fix whose content cannot be read now is ineligible and listed after the pending ones

Step 7.1 F-S71-1: list_user_records reports the identity the custodian resolved the repository path to, the key its grants are authorized by; a directory replaced at the same path has another identity, so the old directory's grant is not its and opens no run; a new grant for the new directory opens a run and its loop is consumed

POST-1 Fix Withdraw (W1, W2, W4, W6, W9, W17, W18): an unconfirmed fix has nothing to withdraw; a guided selection names all four values (MALFORMED_REQUEST otherwise) and the listed confirmation (SELECTION_STALE otherwise), and may locate the repository by its listed identity; the direct form binds the custodian-selected confirmation; the first commit withdraws, a commit prepared before it refuses (recorded nothing) and a prepare after it answers already withdrawn; the application is refused CONFIRMATION_WITHDRAWN before anything else, also after the configuration is revoked and set again, a custodian restart and an OS restart; nothing re-confirms it; a failed content cleanup leaves the fix withdrawn and the sweep removes the content

has: Withdraw the confirmation of delegated fix
A fix applied earlier is not reverted.

scenarios.name: POST-1 Fix Withdraw (W3, W5, W7, W8, W16): withdrawal and consumption from one confirmed state, each one gated write — a withdrawal prepared before an application began refuses CONFIRMATION_CONSUMED at its commit (never success), and an application whose preparatory reads were done when a withdrawal committed is refused CONFIRMATION_WITHDRAWN; an applied, a rejected or a pending fix is refused by its state; an expired confirmation can be withdrawn (already not applicable); a full log refuses a withdrawal and a decision BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and end is still accepted, after which the run has nothing to withdraw

has: It is already not applicable (expired or voided); the withdrawal makes that permanent.
